title: A line of a brain's conversation-history.jsonl
description: One JSON object per line, appended by the bridge, as docs/BRAINS.md describes it. Fields and types are added, never renamed or removed, so a reader ignores the fields and the lines of a type it does not know. This schema describes exactly the lines this version writes, and refuses any other field or type so that tests hold it to the code: a reader validating against it should allow unknown fields and types, as later versions add them.

ts.description: RFC 3339, to the second, with the offset of the bridge's time zone, or Z when the offset is zero (UTC, or London in winter, for one): for an in line when the message was sent, for the others when the line was written.

from.description: in, event and reset: who wrote it, did it or sent !reset, by phone number, or the sender an /ingest named. out: the brain's id; for a line that came in through /send, the brain that sent it or "script" (see via).

chat.description: The chat's JID: a person's number@s.whatsapp.net, or a group's …@g.us.

text.description: What was said, with a quote and attachments as lines of their own; for an event, what happened, after the name in from; empty for a reset.

type.description: in: a message to the brain. out: one it sent, or that was sent for it. event: something that happened in the chat without a message, such as a vote. reset: where !reset started the chat afresh, which a run reads only after.

via.description: How an out line came in through /send: a brain's run token, the scripts token, or no token. A brain's own replies have none.

id.description: The WhatsApp message's id, for a message from WhatsApp, which an edit or deletion names.

otp_request.description: On the out line of a /send that asked for a one-time code: the id the answer of /send gave it, which the hand-off of the code repeats.
